rules.quote: Provide a text alternative to video and audio for:
rules.violation_condition: Video or audio content has no text alternative providing equivalent information.
when: Applies to video and audio content.
The alternative must serve users who cannot reliably read captions or hear audio, as well as users with time pressures.
rules.why: G-2: the listed users and SEO purpose qualify one text-alternative requirement, rather than creating separate checks.

rules.quote: Use words that the user is most likely to type into search engines.
rules.specification: The page does not identify the intended users or their likely search vocabulary. Those must be established for the content being checked.
rules.violation_condition: Tags or hashtags for video content use wording that does not match the intended users’ likely search terms.
when: Applies to words used in tags or hashtags for video content.
rules.why: G-3: choosing to add tags is permitted; once used, their wording is subject to this separate textual requirement.

rules.quote: Include live captioning in synchronised media for live broadcasts to ensure content is available to all users.
rules.violation_condition: A live broadcast using synchronised media lacks live captions.
when: Applies to synchronised media in live broadcasts.

outlines what the content will cover (the beginning)
uses action and audio to show the key idea (the middle)
tells people about what they can do next (the end).
Some video and audio formats are partially scripted. The partial script will outline both the beginning and the end of the content, but might not structure the middle.
For an interview, you might create a conversation outline with a series of questions. Responses and follow-up questions might be unscripted.
You should still write the beginning and end of the content as script.
You should include a call to action so users know what they can do next.

rules.quote: Take the time to create a well-written script with a clear structure.
rules.violation_condition: A script lacks the prescribed beginning, development of the key idea, or ending explaining what users can do next; or a partially scripted production leaves its beginning or end unscripted.
when: Applies to audio-visual and audio-only scripts.

rules.why: The script-role requirement is textual; it is separate from inclusive wording and from the non-text imagery requirement.

rules.quote: Scripts provide clear directions for speakers about emphasis and pronunciation.

covers.quote: When printed or displayed, scripts use:

rules.specification: The page supplies no word, sentence or line threshold for a short paragraph.
rules.violation_condition: A printed or displayed script uses paragraphs that are too long for script reading.

rules.quote: short sentences and some longer sentences to reflect speech patterns
rules.specification: The page does not define short or longer sentences, or the required proportion of each.
rules.violation_condition: A printed or displayed script lacks the mixture of short and longer sentences needed to reflect speech patterns.
when: Applies when a script is printed or displayed.
rules.why: Sentence-length variation requires reading several sentences and is distinct from paragraph length.

rules.quote: markers for brief pauses throughout to help speakers breathe and listeners think
rules.specification: The page does not prescribe marker syntax, pause duration or marker frequency.
rules.violation_condition: A printed or displayed script lacks markers for brief pauses throughout.
when: Applies when a script is printed or displayed.
rules.why: Pause markers are a distinct required feature of the script, not a visual page-setting requirement.

covers.quote: avoid jargon.

rules.violation_condition: Audio-only wording contains unnecessarily complex language or jargon for its intended users.
when: Applies to language in audio-only content.
Simplification must not remove meaning or become patronising.
rules.why: G-4: simple language and avoiding jargon are consolidated as one accessibility-of-wording check; tone is separate.

covers.quote: A conversational tone also helps the speakers inject their personalities into the script.

rules.quote: Use simple language and a conversational tone, and avoid jargon.
rules.violation_condition: Audio-only wording uses a non-conversational tone.
when: Applies to the verbal wording of audio-only content, not the acoustic qualities of a recording.
rules.why: Conversational tone can fail even when vocabulary is simple and jargon-free, so it is a separate check.

rules.quote: Don’t over-simplify to the point where you lose meaning and people feel patronised.
rules.violation_condition: Audio-only wording is simplified so far that it loses meaning or patronises listeners.
when: Applies to language in audio-only content.
rules.why: G-2: loss of meaning and patronising treatment are stated as the boundary on simplification, not permissions to use unnecessarily complex language.
